descriptionChirho: Engraved or inscribed writing, particularly the writing of God on the stone tablets. In Exod 32:16 'the writing was the writing of God (מִכְתַּב אֱלֹהִים) engraved on the tablets,' and the engraved inscription on the high priest's gold plate (Exod 39:30 'a writing of engravings'). Also the similar writing on the second tablets 'according to the writing' (כַּמִּכְתָּב, Deut 10:4). Hezekiah's written prayer/psalm in Isa 38:9 (מִכְתָּב) may also belong here as a formal inscription. All glosses render with writing/écriture/Schrift/लेख/글/كِتابَة, with the construct form מִכְתַּב being an inflectional variant.

A written document, letter, or official decree produced by human hand for communication. In 2 Chr 21:12 a 'writing' (מִכְתָּב) came from Elijah the prophet -- a prophetic letter. In 2 Chr 35:4 and 36:22 official written decrees or documents (בְּמִכְתָּב/וּבְמִכְתַּב) are referenced. Hindi पत्र (letter) and Korean 편지 (letter) in 2 Chr 21:12 confirm the document/correspondence meaning, distinguishing it from the sacred inscription sense. Also rendered as 'escrito/écrit/writing' in the European translations.
